# Use a standard Ubuntu LTS release as the base image
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package managers
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, LAMMPS prerequisites, and certificates.
# Added python3 and python3-dev to fix CMake dependency error.
# Clean up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    libfftw3-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    libgomp1 \
    python3 \
    python3-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set OpenMPI environment variables to allow running as root, which is common in containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1

# Create a temporary directory for the build process.
# This entire process is done in a single RUN command to minimize layer size by
# ensuring the source code and build artifacts are not stored in the final image.
RUN mkdir /tmp/build && cd /tmp/build && \
    # Clone the latest development branch of the LAMMPS source code as instructed.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch develop https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git . && \
    # Create a build directory
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake. Enable MPI and the REAXFF package.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
      ../cmake && \
    # Compile LAMMPS using all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a location in the system's PATH
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/lmp && \
    # Create the application work directory and copy the required example files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp /tmp/build/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    # Clean up the build directory to keep the final image clean
    cd / && rm -rf /tmp/build

# Set the working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Set the default entrypoint to the LAMMPS executable.
# Users can append input files and arguments at runtime (e.g., docker run image -in in.hns)
ENTRYPOINT ["lmp"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation
# for testing purposes on a single AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster.
# It is configured to be deployed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-test
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Specify the size of the MiniCluster, which corresponds to the number of pods.
  # For this single-node test, we set the size to 1.
  size: 1

  # The total number of tasks to be launched by Flux.
  # As this is a simple test on one node, we will run one task.
  tasks: 1

  # The container that will run the LAMMPS simulation.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by the Flux framework.
      # The Flux Operator will automatically wrap this with 'flux run'.
      # This runs the 'in.reaxff.hns' input file with specified variables.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the job.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures strict schema validation for the CRD.
    strict: true

  # Set cleanup to false to keep the pods running after the job completes
  # for debugging and inspection purposes.
  cleanup: false

This attempt will establish a new performance baseline on a high-core-count, HPC-optimized ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) to explore a different architecture. The number of tasks is set to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the selected node.

The previous run on the ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance yielded a massive performance improvement (FOM: 723.261). This attempt will switch to a high-core-count, compute-optimized AMD instance (c7a.12xlarge) to compare x86 performance at scale. The task count is adjusted to 48 to match the vCPU count of the new instance.

The previous attempts have tested the best available instances from each CPU architecture (ARM, AMD, Intel). The ARM-based hpc7g.16xlarge instance provided a significantly higher Figure of Merit (723.261) than both the AMD (584.188) and subsequent Intel tests. This indicates that for this LAMMPS workload, the higher core count of the Graviton3 CPU on an HPC-optimized node is the dominant factor for performance. Further trials on lower-spec instances are unlikely to yield a better result. The optimization is complete.
